content_html:
Let's design the successor to email on top of HTTP, fixing the design flaws SMTP has been dragging along for 40 years. Piece by piece. The goal is not to replace the current mail system, heaven forbid!, but to learn, have fun and discover current technologies to swap out every element: sending, receiving, gateway, keys, and so on. The system will never talk to Gmail or any classic email provider: it only talks to itself. The only thing we are going to keep is the shape of the addresses, user@domain. Everything else gets reinvented.

Since it is a mail system over HTTP, a good name for the protocol would be HMTP: Hypertext Mail Transfer Protocol (the S for Simple in SMTP gives up its seat to the H for HTTP).

Now it's time to prepare the tech stack: HTTP, TLS, WebFinger, ActivityPub, Webmention, Ed25519, HPKE, sigchains, etc.

The bill of materials

This design doesn't invent a single technology: everything already exists.

Problem Existing technology Who uses it today
Transport and status codes HTTP The whole web
Transport encryption TLS + Let's Encrypt The whole web
User discovery WebFinger (RFC 7033) Mastodon and the Fediverse
Message delivery POST to an inbox ActivityPub
Sender verification at the source The Webmention and DKIM pattern IndieWeb, all of email
Signatures Ed25519 SSH, Signal
Content encryption HPKE (RFC 9180) MLS, TLS ECH
Identity that survives key rotation Sigchains ATProto (Bluesky), Keybase
Reading and synchronization JMAP (RFC 8620) Fastmail
Push notifications SSE / WebPush Every browser
First-contact consent Message requests Signal, Instagram
Attachments by reference with hashes Content addressing Git, IPFS, Matrix

Every piece we are going to use is standardized, deployed and battle-tested at scale by millions of people; the only new thing is the assembly.

Choosing HTTP is not just pragmatism. It solves, right out of the gate, several things any new protocol would have to build at some point:

  • TLS, virtual hosting and SNI: for free.
  • Status codes: the catalog a mail protocol needs already exists in HTTP. 202 Accepted (queued for delivery), 429 Too Many Requests + Retry-After (rate control), 404/410 (mailbox unknown/gone), 3xx (mailbox moved), 413 (too large). Even paid anti-spam has had a code reserved since 1997: 402 Payment Required.
  • Existing infrastructure: proxies, load balancers, Nginx, libraries in every language. The protocol stops being a new server and becomes a convention over HTTP, like Webmention or Micropub.

Let's move to the next level: how do we discover a user, verify their identity, deliver the message, sign it and encrypt it, all over HTTP?

1. Discovery and delegation (a better MX)

Delegation is solved with a static document:

GET https://example.com/.well-known/hmtp/ana
{
  "inbox": "https://mail.migadu.example/hmtp/inbox/ana",
  "keys": { ... },
  "devices": [ ... ]
}

The inbox can live on another host: that is the MX record, but without touching DNS. A static blog on GitHub Pages can delegate its mail to a provider by serving a JSON file. And it allows something MX never did: per-user delegation (each mailbox of a domain on a different provider). We wouldn't even need to invent the route: WebFinger (RFC 7033) does exactly this, and Mastodon has already proven it scales.

2. Identity that survives key rotation

Identity cannot be a key (they get lost, they expire); it has to be something that keys back. A proposal with two anchors:

  • Cryptographic continuity: the discovery document publishes the current key and a chain of rotations, where each new key is signed by the previous one. Anyone who knew you with key N can verify key N+1 without trusting anybody. It's a sigchain, what ATProto does with DIDs or what Keybase used to do.
  • Domain control as a fallback: if you lose the key without a signed rotation (your laptop gets stolen), the domain declares a new key without a chain, with a mandatory announcement period (say 30 days) during which the servers that knew you show the warning "identity re-anchored by domain, not by signature".

However, domain-anchored identity has its own Achilles heel: a domain is not owned, it is rented. If you stop paying, it expires and someone registers it, the new owner publishes their keys in your .well-known and from that moment on they receive your mail and sign as you. Nobody can tell the legitimate heir from the squatter. It's the problem ATProto tries to solve by separating identity from the domain with DIDs, at the price of another piece of infrastructure. We know it's a real problem with a known solution. Now let's move on.

3. Delivery with a queue (store-and-forward)

Delivery is a POST to the recipient's inbox:

POST /hmtp/inbox/ana HTTP/1.1
Host: mail.migadu.example
Content-Type: application/hmtp+json

The key is not the request, it's who makes it. Your client doesn't deliver directly to the recipient, but to your own server (an authenticated POST to your outbox), and it is your server that queues, retries with exponential backoff and honors Retry-After. It's admitting that SMTP's MUA/MSA/MTA separation was right. One of email's quiet strokes of genius is that if the destination server is down, your server retries for days and you forget about it.

But let's add an improvement SMTP never had. Every message carries an ID that is the hash of its content, so retries are idempotent. The receiving server deduplicates by ID and the classic "duplicate email because the ACK failed" disappears by construction.

The full cycle of a delivery, with the destination node down on the first attempt:

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Ana as Ana's client
    participant SA as Ana's server
    participant SB as Bob's server

    Ana->>SA: POST /outbox (signed message)
    SA-->>Ana: 202 queued
    SA->>SB: GET /.well-known/hmtp/bob
    SB-->>SA: Bob's inbox and keys
    SA->>SB: POST /hmtp/inbox/bob (envelope + sealed body)
    Note over SB: down: no response
    Note over SA: queue: retries with exponential backoff
    SA->>SB: POST /hmtp/inbox/bob (retry, same id)
    SB->>SA: GET /.well-known/hmtp/ana
    SA-->>SB: Ana's signing key
    Note over SB: signature verified, deduplicated by id
    SB-->>SA: 201 delivered

Notice that the diagram contains the entire protocol: the two GETs to .well-known are discovery and verification, the POST is the delivery, and the queue lives where it should, on the sender's server.

4. Signing and encrypting with the keys we already have

The message is a signed object, not loose text:

{
  "id": "sha256:9f2c...",
  "from": "ana@example.com",
  "to": ["bruno@example.org"],
  "date": "2026-07-26T10:00:00Z",
  "in_reply_to": "sha256:11ab...",
  "subject": "Re: that idea",
  "body": { "type": "text/markdown", "content": "<encrypted>" },
  "signature": "..."
}

This buys us a lot of things:

  • Authenticity at rest: stored mail carries its cryptographic proof. A forward keeps the original signature. Forging the sender becomes impossible even through chains of forwards.
  • Sender verification without DKIM: the receiving server GETs the .well-known of the from domain and checks that the key signs. It's the same move as Webmention verification. The proof is fetched at the source.
  • E2E: the discovery document publishes encryption keys (X25519); the body is sealed with HPKE. The envelope (from, to, id, date) stays visible for routing and filtering; the content, only for the recipient.
  • Threads: in_reply_to and references by content hash. Conversations reconstructed without heuristics.
  • Attachments: outside the message. An attachment is {hash, url, size} pointing to the sender's server; the receiver downloads it on demand and their server can mirror it. No more base64 bloating mailboxes.

5. Layered anti-spam

Like in any system, this is a complex problem that needs several layers of defense. With HMTP we could start with three:

  1. Identity cost: signing as ana@example.com requires serving the key document at example.com. Identity is anchored to a domain, and domains cost money. It's the sybil cost that self-signed identities don't have. However, a domain gives you infinite subdomains and mailboxes, so the cost slows down the mass creation of independent identities, not of addresses. We work at the root level.
  2. First-contact consent: an unknown sender doesn't get into the mailbox; they land in a "requests" box with their first message visible (like Signal's message requests). You accept, and the thread opens forever. A stranger can knock on your door, which is the essential property of mail, but they can't fill up your living room.
  3. Optional postage for strangers: the server can answer a first contact with a 402. Configurable per mailbox; the cost of cold spamming stops being zero.

6. Reading gets specified too

Email standardized sending (SMTP) and reading (IMAP/POP) as separate worlds. We don't need to invent anything: reading, synchronizing and searching mailboxes over JSON/HTTP is already solved and standardized by the IETF. It's called JMAP. HMTP would define delivery; reading is JMAP with one new object type. Push to the client with SSE or WebPush. The full cycle (send, deliver, read, sync) stays on HTTP.

The conclusion

Every problem of email has a solution deployed and working: discovery in Mastodon, delivery in ActivityPub, verification in the IndieWeb, rotatable identity in Bluesky, reading in Fastmail, consent in Signal. An upgrade to email already exists, but nobody has assembled it.

We solve many problems with elegant, modern solutions:

  • Reputation and social permission (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, reverse PTR, blocklists, months of warming up an IP): replaced by cryptographic verification on every message, one signature and one GET to the sender's .well-known. A property that can be verified doesn't need reputation.
  • Sender spoofing: impossible by construction. The receiver checks the signature against the key published on the from domain, and the signature travels with the message even when forwarded.
  • Mail delegation (the MX record): a static document in .well-known, with per-user delegation and no DNS changes.
  • Content privacy (the PGP nobody ever got around to configuring): end-to-end encryption by default; the receiving server stores a body it cannot read.
  • Spam (statistical filters after the fact): first-contact consent (strangers knock on the door, they don't walk into the mailbox), costly identity anchored to a domain, and optional postage with 402.
  • Duplicates on retry: the message id is the hash of its content, so retries are idempotent and the receiver deduplicates by construction.
  • Threads rebuilt with heuristics: in_reply_to points to the hash of the parent message; the conversation is a verifiable graph.
  • Light mailboxes: attachments by reference (hash + URL), downloaded on demand.
  • Simple, familiar infrastructure: everything travels over standard HTTPS, behind the same Nginx and the same certificate that already serve your website.
  • Key rotation (DKIM's operational nightmare): one command. Since nobody pins your key, the new one is trusted instantly and the stolen one becomes useless just as fast.

Talk is cheap, so I implemented a working prototype in Python: github.com/tanrax/hmtp. All in a single file. The prototype covers the full transport: signed delivery, verification at the source, end-to-end encryption, first-contact consent, deduplication, threads, a queue with exponential backoff and key rotation in one command. It deliberately leaves out the pieces at the periphery: the chain of signed rotations (receivers fetch your key live on every delivery instead of pinning it, so the chain only starts paying off once nodes cache keys), the 402 postage, attachments by reference and JMAP reading. The README has the quickstart (your first message in two minutes, mailing yourself), a demo of two nodes exchanging encrypted mail on your machine, and the full production guide, from DNS to systemd. Remember it's a design experiment with unaudited cryptography; don't use it for secrets anyone depends on. Although it could be a lightweight communication system for whatever ecosystem comes to your mind.

I hope you enjoyed the ride. And if you ever send your first HMTP message, I'd love to hear about it.

blocks.html_en: Choosing HTTP is not just pragmatism. It solves, right out of the gate, several things any new protocol would have to build at some point:

sentences.en: Choosing HTTP is not just pragmatism.
sentences.zh: 选择HTTP不仅仅是实用主义。

sentences.en: It solves, right out of the gate, several things any new protocol would have to build at some point:
sentences.zh: 它立即解决了任何新协议在某个时刻都必须构建的几件事：

blocks.html_en: • TLS, virtual hosting and SNI: for free.

sentences.en: TLS, virtual hosting and SNI: for free.

blocks.html_en: • Status codes: the catalog a mail protocol needs already exists in HTTP. 202 Accepted (queued for delivery), 429 Too Many Requests + Retry-After (rate control), 404/410 (mailbox unknown/gone), 3xx (mailbox moved), 413 (too large). Even paid anti-spam has had a code reserved since 1997: 402 Payment Required.

sentences.en: Status codes: the catalog a mail protocol needs already exists in HTTP.
sentences.zh: 状态码：邮件协议所需的目录已存在于 HTTP 中。

sentences.en: 202 Accepted (queued for delivery), 429 Too Many Requests + Retry-After (rate control), 404/410 (mailbox unknown/gone), 3xx (mailbox moved), 413 (too large).
sentences.zh: 202 已接受（排队等待传送）、429 请求过多 + 之后重试（速率控制）、404/410（邮箱未知/消失）、3xx（邮箱已移动）、413（太大）。

sentences.en: Even paid anti-spam has had a code reserved since 1997: 402 Payment Required.
sentences.zh: 即使是付费的反垃圾邮件，自 1997 年以来也保留了一个代码：402 需要付款。

blocks.html_en: • Existing infrastructure: proxies, load balancers, Nginx, libraries in every language. The protocol stops being a new server and becomes a convention over HTTP, like Webmention or Micropub.

sentences.en: Existing infrastructure: proxies, load balancers, Nginx, libraries in every language.
sentences.zh: 现有基础设施：代理、负载均衡器、Nginx、各种语言的库。

sentences.zh: 该协议不再是一个新的服务器，而是成为 HTTP 上的约定，如 Webmention 或 Micropub。

blocks.html_en: 1. Discovery and delegation (a better MX)

sentences.en: Discovery and delegation (a better MX)
sentences.zh: 发现和委派（更好的 MX）

blocks.html_en: Delegation is solved with a static document:

sentences.en: Delegation is solved with a static document:
sentences.zh: 委托是通过静态文件解决的：

blocks.html_en: The inbox can live on another host: that is the MX record, but without touching DNS. A static blog on GitHub Pages can delegate its mail to a provider by serving a JSON file. And it allows something MX never did: per-user delegation (each mailbox of a domain on a different provider). We wouldn't even need to invent the route: WebFinger (RFC 7033) does exactly this, and Mastodon has already proven it scales.

sentences.en: The inbox can live on another host: that is the MX record, but without touching DNS.
sentences.zh: 收件箱可以驻留在另一台主机上：即 MX 记录，但不涉及 DNS。

sentences.en: A static blog on GitHub Pages can delegate its mail to a provider by serving a JSON file.
sentences.zh: GitHub Pages 上的静态博客可以通过提供 JSON 文件将其邮件委托给提供商。

sentences.en: And it allows something MX never did: per-user delegation (each mailbox of a domain on a different provider).
sentences.zh: 它允许 MX 从未做过的事情：每用户委托（不同提供商的域的每个邮箱）。

sentences.en: We wouldn't even need to invent the route: WebFinger (RFC 7033) does exactly this, and Mastodon has already proven it scales.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至不需要发明路线：WebFinger (RFC 7033) 正是这样做的，并且 Mastodon 已经证明了它的可扩展性。

blocks.html_en: 2. Identity that survives key rotation

sentences.en: Identity that survives key rotation
sentences.zh: 在密钥轮换后仍然存在的身份

blocks.html_en: Identity cannot be a key (they get lost, they expire); it has to be something that keys back. A proposal with two anchors:

sentences.en: Identity cannot be a key (they get lost, they expire); it has to be something that keys back.
sentences.zh: 身份不能成为钥匙（它们会丢失、过期）；它必须是可以按键返回的东西。

sentences.en: A proposal with two anchors:
sentences.zh: 具有两个锚点的提案：

blocks.html_en: • Cryptographic continuity: the discovery document publishes the current key and a chain of rotations, where each new key is signed by the previous one. Anyone who knew you with key N can verify key N+1 without trusting anybody. It's a sigchain, what ATProto does with DIDs or what Keybase used to do.

sentences.en: Cryptographic continuity: the discovery document publishes the current key and a chain of rotations, where each new key is signed by the previous one.
sentences.zh: 加密连续性：发现文档发布当前密钥和一系列轮换，其中每个新密钥都由前一个密钥签名。

sentences.en: Anyone who knew you with key N can verify key N+1 without trusting anybody.
sentences.zh: 任何认识你并拥有密钥 N 的人都可以验证密钥 N+1，而无需信任任何人。

sentences.en: It's a sigchain, what ATProto does with DIDs or what Keybase used to do.
sentences.zh: 它是一个信号链，类似于 ATProto 对 DID 所做的事情或 Keybase 过去所做的事情。

blocks.html_en: • Domain control as a fallback: if you lose the key without a signed rotation (your laptop gets stolen), the domain declares a new key without a chain, with a mandatory announcement period (say 30 days) during which the servers that knew you show the warning "identity re-anchored by domain, not by signature".

sentences.en: Domain control as a fallback: if you lose the key without a signed rotation (your laptop gets stolen), the domain declares a new key without a chain, with a mandatory announcement period (say 30 days) during which the servers that knew you show the warning "identity re-anchored by domain, not by signature".
sentences.zh: 域控制作为后备：如果您在没有签名轮换的情况下丢失密钥（您的笔记本电脑被盗），域会声明一个没有链的新密钥，并有一个强制公告期（例如 30 天），在此期间，知道您的服务器会显示警告“通过域重新锚定身份，而不是通过签名”。

blocks.html_en: However, domain-anchored identity has its own Achilles heel: a domain is not owned, it is rented. If you stop paying, it expires and someone registers it, the new owner publishes their keys in your .well-known and from that moment on they receive your mail and sign as you. Nobody can tell the legitimate heir from the squatter. It's the problem ATProto tries to solve by separating identity from the domain with DIDs, at the price of another piece of infrastructure. We know it's a real problem with a known solution. Now let's move on.

sentences.en: However, domain-anchored identity has its own Achilles heel: a domain is not owned, it is rented.
sentences.zh: 然而，域名锚定身份有其自身的致命弱点：域名不是拥有的，而是租用的。

sentences.en: If you stop paying, it expires and someone registers it, the new owner publishes their keys in your .well-known and from that moment on they receive your mail and sign as you.
sentences.zh: 如果您停止付款，它就会过期并且有人注册，新所有者会在您的 .well-known 中发布他们的密钥，从那一刻起，他们会收到您的邮件并以您的身份签名。

sentences.en: Nobody can tell the legitimate heir from the squatter.
sentences.zh: 没有人能区分合法继承人和擅自占地者。

sentences.en: It's the problem ATProto tries to solve by separating identity from the domain with DIDs, at the price of another piece of infrastructure.
sentences.zh: ATProto 试图通过使用 DID 将身份与域分离来解决这个问题，但代价是另一块基础设施。

sentences.en: We know it's a real problem with a known solution.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这是一个已知解决方案的实际问题。

sentences.en: Now let's move on.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们继续吧。

blocks.html_en: 3. Delivery with a queue (store-and-forward)

sentences.en: Delivery with a queue (store-and-forward)
sentences.zh: 使用队列传送（存储转发）

blocks.html_en: Delivery is a POST to the recipient's inbox:

sentences.en: Delivery is a POST to the recipient's inbox:
sentences.zh: 投递是通过 POST 方式发送到收件人的收件箱：

blocks.html_en: The key is not the request, it's who makes it. Your client doesn't deliver directly to the recipient, but to your own server (an authenticated POST to your outbox), and it is your server that queues, retries with exponential backoff and honors Retry-After. It's admitting that SMTP's MUA/MSA/MTA separation was right. One of email's quiet strokes of genius is that if the destination server is down, your server retries for days and you forget about it.

sentences.en: The key is not the request, it's who makes it.
sentences.zh: 关键不在于请求，而在于提出请求的人。

sentences.en: Your client doesn't deliver directly to the recipient, but to your own server (an authenticated POST to your outbox), and it is your server that queues, retries with exponential backoff and honors Retry-After.
sentences.zh: 您的客户端不会直接发送给收件人，而是发送给您自己的服务器（经过身份验证的 POST 到您的发件箱），并且您的服务器进行排队、以指数退避重试并遵循“重试后”。

sentences.en: It's admitting that SMTP's MUA/MSA/MTA separation was right.
sentences.zh: 承认SMTP的MUA/MSA/MTA分离是正确的。

sentences.en: One of email's quiet strokes of genius is that if the destination server is down, your server retries for days and you forget about it.
sentences.zh: 电子邮件的巧妙之处之一是，如果目标服务器出现故障，您的服务器会重试数天，然后您就会忘记它。

blocks.html_en: But let's add an improvement SMTP never had. Every message carries an ID that is the hash of its content, so retries are idempotent. The receiving server deduplicates by ID and the classic "duplicate email because the ACK failed" disappears by construction.

sentences.en: But let's add an improvement SMTP never had.
sentences.zh: 但让我们添加一个 SMTP 从未有过的改进。

sentences.en: Every message carries an ID that is the hash of its content, so retries are idempotent.
sentences.zh: 每条消息都带有一个 ID，该 ID 是其内容的哈希值，因此重试是幂等的。

sentences.en: The receiving server deduplicates by ID and the classic "duplicate email because the ACK failed" disappears by construction.
sentences.zh: 接收服务器通过 ID 进行重复数据删除，经典的“由于 ACK 失败而导致重复的电子邮件”通过构建而消失。

blocks.html_en: The full cycle of a delivery, with the destination node down on the first attempt:

sentences.en: The full cycle of a delivery, with the destination node down on the first attempt:
sentences.zh: 交付的完整周期，目标节点在第一次尝试时关闭：

blocks.html_en: Notice that the diagram contains the entire protocol: the two GETs to .well-known are discovery and verification, the POST is the delivery, and the queue lives where it should, on the sender's server.

sentences.en: Notice that the diagram contains the entire protocol: the two GETs to .well-known are discovery and verification, the POST is the delivery, and the queue lives where it should, on the sender's server.
sentences.zh: 请注意，该图包含整个协议：.wellknown 的两个 GET 是发现和验证，POST 是传递，队列位于发送者服务器上应有的位置。

blocks.html_en: 4. Signing and encrypting with the keys we already have

sentences.en: Signing and encrypting with the keys we already have
sentences.zh: 使用我们已有的密钥进行签名和加密

blocks.html_en: The message is a signed object, not loose text:

sentences.en: The message is a signed object, not loose text:
sentences.zh: 该消息是一个签名对象，而不是松散的文本：

blocks.html_en: This buys us a lot of things:

sentences.en: This buys us a lot of things:
sentences.zh: 这给我们带来了很多东西：

blocks.html_en: • Authenticity at rest: stored mail carries its cryptographic proof. A forward keeps the original signature. Forging the sender becomes impossible even through chains of forwards.

sentences.en: Authenticity at rest: stored mail carries its cryptographic proof.
sentences.zh: 静态真实性：存储的邮件带有其加密证明。

sentences.en: A forward keeps the original signature.
sentences.zh: 转发者保留原始签名。

sentences.en: Forging the sender becomes impossible even through chains of forwards.
sentences.zh: 即使通过转发链，伪造发送者也是不可能的。

blocks.html_en: • Sender verification without DKIM: the receiving server GETs the .well-known of the from domain and checks that the key signs. It's the same move as Webmention verification. The proof is fetched at the source.

sentences.en: Sender verification without DKIM: the receiving server GETs the .well-known of the from domain and checks that the key signs.
sentences.zh: 无需 DKIM 的发件人验证：接收服务器获取来自域的 .wellknown 并检查密钥签名。

sentences.en: It's the same move as Webmention verification.
sentences.zh: 和Webmention验证的动作是一样的。

sentences.en: The proof is fetched at the source.
sentences.zh: 证据是从源头获取的。

blocks.html_en: • E2E: the discovery document publishes encryption keys (X25519); the body is sealed with HPKE. The envelope (from, to, id, date) stays visible for routing and filtering; the content, only for the recipient.

sentences.en: E2E: the discovery document publishes encryption keys (X25519); the body is sealed with HPKE.
sentences.zh: E2E：发现文档公开加密密钥（X25519）；本体采用 HPKE 密封。

sentences.en: The envelope (from, to, id, date) stays visible for routing and filtering; the content, only for the recipient.
sentences.zh: 信封（发件人、收件人、id、日期）对于路由和过滤保持可见；内容仅供收件人使用。

blocks.html_en: • Threads: in_reply_to and references by content hash. Conversations reconstructed without heuristics.

sentences.en: Threads: in_reply_to and references by content hash.
sentences.zh: 线程：in_reply_to 和内容哈希引用。

sentences.en: Conversations reconstructed without heuristics.
sentences.zh: 无需启发式即可重建对话。

blocks.html_en: • Attachments: outside the message. An attachment is {hash, url, size} pointing to the sender's server; the receiver downloads it on demand and their server can mirror it. No more base64 bloating mailboxes.

sentences.en: Attachments: outside the message.
sentences.zh: 附件：邮件外。

sentences.en: An attachment is {hash, url, size} pointing to the sender's server; the receiver downloads it on demand and their server can mirror it.
sentences.zh: 附件是指向发件人服务器的{hash, url, size}；接收者按需下载它，他们的服务器可以镜像它。

sentences.en: No more base64 bloating mailboxes.
sentences.zh: 不再有 Base64 膨胀的邮箱。

blocks.html_en: 5. Layered anti-spam

sentences.en: Layered anti-spam
sentences.zh: 分层反垃圾邮件

blocks.html_en: Like in any system, this is a complex problem that needs several layers of defense. With HMTP we could start with three:

sentences.en: Like in any system, this is a complex problem that needs several layers of defense.
sentences.zh: 与任何系统一样，这是一个复杂的问题，需要多层防御。

sentences.en: With HMTP we could start with three:
sentences.zh: 对于 HMTP，我们可以从三个开始：

blocks.html_en: • Identity cost: signing as ana@example.com requires serving the key document at example.com. Identity is anchored to a domain, and domains cost money. It's the sybil cost that self-signed identities don't have. However, a domain gives you infinite subdomains and mailboxes, so the cost slows down the mass creation of independent identities, not of addresses. We work at the root level.

sentences.en: Identity cost: signing as ana@example.com requires serving the key document at example.com.
sentences.zh: 身份成本：以 ana@example.com 身份签名需要在 example.com 上提供密钥文档。

sentences.en: Identity is anchored to a domain, and domains cost money.
sentences.zh: 身份锚定于域名，而域名需要花钱。

sentences.en: It's the sybil cost that self-signed identities don't have.
sentences.zh: 这是自签名身份所没有的女巫成本。

sentences.en: However, a domain gives you infinite subdomains and mailboxes, so the cost slows down the mass creation of independent identities, not of addresses.
sentences.zh: 但是，域为您提供了无限的子域和邮箱，因此成本会减慢独立身份（而不是地址）的大规模创建速度。

sentences.en: We work at the root level.
sentences.zh: 我们在根部层面开展工作。

blocks.html_en: • First-contact consent: an unknown sender doesn't get into the mailbox; they land in a "requests" box with their first message visible (like Signal's message requests). You accept, and the thread opens forever. A stranger can knock on your door, which is the essential property of mail, but they can't fill up your living room.

sentences.en: First-contact consent: an unknown sender doesn't get into the mailbox; they land in a "requests" box with their first message visible (like Signal's message requests).
sentences.zh: 首次联系同意：未知发件人不会进入邮箱；他们降落在“请求”框中，其中第一条消息可见（如 Signal 的消息请求）。

sentences.en: You accept, and the thread opens forever.
sentences.zh: 您接受，该线程将永远打开。

sentences.en: A stranger can knock on your door, which is the essential property of mail, but they can't fill up your living room.
sentences.zh: 陌生人可以敲你的门，这是邮件的基本属性，但他们不能填满你的客厅。

blocks.html_en: • Optional postage for strangers: the server can answer a first contact with a 402. Configurable per mailbox; the cost of cold spamming stops being zero.

sentences.en: Optional postage for strangers: the server can answer a first contact with a 402.
sentences.zh: 陌生人可选邮资：服务器可以回复 402 的第一次联系。

sentences.en: Configurable per mailbox; the cost of cold spamming stops being zero.
sentences.zh: 每个邮箱均可配置；冷垃圾邮件的成本不再为零。

blocks.html_en: 6. Reading gets specified too

sentences.en: Reading gets specified too
sentences.zh: 阅读也被指定

blocks.html_en: Email standardized sending (SMTP) and reading (IMAP/POP) as separate worlds. We don't need to invent anything: reading, synchronizing and searching mailboxes over JSON/HTTP is already solved and standardized by the IETF. It's called JMAP. HMTP would define delivery; reading is JMAP with one new object type. Push to the client with SSE or WebPush. The full cycle (send, deliver, read, sync) stays on HTTP.

sentences.en: Email standardized sending (SMTP) and reading (IMAP/POP) as separate worlds.
sentences.zh: 电子邮件标准化发送 (SMTP) 和阅读 (IMAP/POP) 作为独立的世界。

sentences.en: We don't need to invent anything: reading, synchronizing and searching mailboxes over JSON/HTTP is already solved and standardized by the IETF.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要发明任何东西：通过 JSON/HTTP 读取、同步和搜索邮箱已经由 IETF 解决和标准化。

sentences.en: It's called JMAP.
sentences.zh: 它称为 JMAP。

sentences.en: HMTP would define delivery; reading is JMAP with one new object type.
sentences.zh: HMTP 将定义交付；读取的是带有一种新对象类型的 JMAP。

sentences.en: Push to the client with SSE or WebPush.
sentences.zh: 使用SSE或WebPush推送到客户端。

sentences.en: The full cycle (send, deliver, read, sync) stays on HTTP.
sentences.zh: 完整的周期（发送、交付、读取、同步）保留在 HTTP 上。

blocks.html_en: The conclusion

sentences.en: The conclusion
sentences.zh: 结论

blocks.html_en: Every problem of email has a solution deployed and working: discovery in Mastodon, delivery in ActivityPub, verification in the IndieWeb, rotatable identity in Bluesky, reading in Fastmail, consent in Signal. An upgrade to email already exists, but nobody has assembled it.

sentences.en: Every problem of email has a solution deployed and working: discovery in Mastodon, delivery in ActivityPub, verification in the IndieWeb, rotatable identity in Bluesky, reading in Fastmail, consent in Signal.
sentences.zh: 电子邮件的每个问题都有一个已部署且有效的解决方案：Mastodon 中的发现、ActivityPub 中的传递、IndieWeb 中的验证、Bluesky 中的可轮换身份、Fastmail 中的阅读、Signal 中的同意。

sentences.en: An upgrade to email already exists, but nobody has assembled it.
sentences.zh: 电子邮件的升级已经存在，但没有人组装它。

blocks.html_en: We solve many problems with elegant, modern solutions:

sentences.en: We solve many problems with elegant, modern solutions:
sentences.zh: 我们通过优雅、现代的解决方案解决了许多问题：

blocks.html_en: • Reputation and social permission (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, reverse PTR, blocklists, months of warming up an IP): replaced by cryptographic verification on every message, one signature and one GET to the sender's .well-known. A property that can be verified doesn't need reputation.

sentences.en: Reputation and social permission (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, reverse PTR, blocklists, months of warming up an IP): replaced by cryptographic verification on every message, one signature and one GET to the sender's .well-known.
sentences.zh: 声誉和社交许可（SPF、DKIM、DMARC、反向 PTR、阻止列表、IP 预热数月）：由每条消息的加密验证、一个签名和一个 GET 到发件人的 .well-known 所取代。

sentences.en: A property that can be verified doesn't need reputation.
sentences.zh: 可以验证的财产不需要声誉。

blocks.html_en: • Sender spoofing: impossible by construction. The receiver checks the signature against the key published on the from domain, and the signature travels with the message even when forwarded.

sentences.en: Sender spoofing: impossible by construction.

content_html_zh:
让我们在 HTTP 之上设计电子邮件的后继者，修复 SMTP 40 年来一直存在的设计缺陷。 一点一点。 我们的目标不是取代当前的邮件系统（但愿不会！），而是学习、享受乐趣并发现当前的技术来替换每个元素：发送、接收、网关、密钥等等。 该系统永远不会与 Gmail 或任何传统电子邮件提供商对话：它只会与自己对话。 我们唯一要保留的是地址的形式，user@domain。 其他一切都被重新发明。

由于它是基于 HTTP 的邮件系统，因此该协议的一个好名称是 HMTP：超文本邮件传输协议（SMTP 中的 S（简单）将其席位让给了 H（HTTP））。

现在是时候准备技术堆栈了：HTTP、TLS、WebFinger、ActivityPub、Webmention、Ed25519、HPKE、sigchains 等。

物料清单

这种设计并没有发明任何一项技术：一切都已经存在。

问题 现有技术 今天谁使用它
传输和状态代码 HTTP 整个网络
传输加密 TLS + 让我们加密 整个网络
用户发现 WebFinger (RFC 7033) 乳齿象与联邦宇宙
消息传递 发布到收件箱 活动酒吧
从源头验证发件人 Webmention 和 DKIM 模式 IndieWeb，所有电子邮件
签名 Ed25519 SSH、信号
内容加密 HPKE (RFC 9180) MLS、TLS ECH
在密钥轮换后仍然存在的身份 信号链 ATProto (Bluesky)、Keybase
读取和同步 JMAP（RFC 8620） 快速邮件
推送通知 上交所/网络推送 每个浏览器
首次接触同意 留言请求 信号、Instagram
通过哈希值引用附件 内容寻址 Git、IPFS、矩阵

我们将要使用的每一件产品都经过数百万人的标准化、大规模部署和实战测试；唯一的新事物是大会。

选择HTTP不仅仅是实用主义。 它立即解决了任何新协议在某个时刻都必须构建的几件事：

  • TLS、虚拟主机和 SNI：免费。
  • 状态码：邮件协议所需的目录已存在于 HTTP 中。 202 已接受（排队等待传送）、429 请求过多 + 之后重试（速率控制）、404/410（邮箱未知/消失）、3xx（邮箱已移动）、413（太大）。 即使是付费的反垃圾邮件，自 1997 年以来也保留了一个代码：402 需要付款。
  • 现有基础设施：代理、负载均衡器、Nginx、各种语言的库。 该协议不再是一个新的服务器，而是成为 HTTP 上的约定，如 Webmention 或 Micropub。

让我们进入下一个层次：我们如何通过 HTTP 发现用户、验证其身份、传递消息、对其进行签名和加密？

1. 发现和委派（更好的 MX）

委托是通过静态文件解决的：

GET https://example.com/.well-known/hmtp/ana
{
  "inbox": "https://mail.migadu.example/hmtp/inbox/ana",
  "keys": { ... },
  "devices": [ ... ]
}

收件箱可以驻留在另一台主机上：即 MX 记录，但不涉及 DNS。 GitHub Pages 上的静态博客可以通过提供 JSON 文件将其邮件委托给提供商。 它允许 MX 从未做过的事情：每用户委托（不同提供商的域的每个邮箱）。 我们甚至不需要发明路线：WebFinger (RFC 7033) 正是这样做的，并且 Mastodon 已经证明了它的可扩展性。

2. 在密钥轮换后仍然存在的身份

身份不能成为钥匙（它们会丢失、过期）；它必须是可以按键返回的东西。 具有两个锚点的提案：

  • 加密连续性：发现文档发布当前密钥和一系列轮换，其中每个新密钥都由前一个密钥签名。 任何认识你并拥有密钥 N 的人都可以验证密钥 N+1，而无需信任任何人。 它是一个信号链，类似于 ATProto 对 DID 所做的事情或 Keybase 过去所做的事情。
  • 域控制作为后备：如果您在没有签名轮换的情况下丢失密钥（您的笔记本电脑被盗），域会声明一个没有链的新密钥，并有一个强制公告期（例如 30 天），在此期间，知道您的服务器会显示警告“通过域重新锚定身份，而不是通过签名”。

然而，域名锚定身份有其自身的致命弱点：域名不是拥有的，而是租用的。 如果您停止付款，它就会过期并且有人注册，新所有者会在您的 .well-known 中发布他们的密钥，从那一刻起，他们会收到您的邮件并以您的身份签名。 没有人能区分合法继承人和擅自占地者。 ATProto 试图通过使用 DID 将身份与域分离来解决这个问题，但代价是另一块基础设施。 我们知道这是一个已知解决方案的实际问题。 现在让我们继续吧。

3. 使用队列传送（存储转发）

投递是通过 POST 方式发送到收件人的收件箱：

POST /hmtp/inbox/ana HTTP/1.1
Host: mail.migadu.example
Content-Type: application/hmtp+json

关键不在于请求，而在于提出请求的人。 您的客户端不会直接发送给收件人，而是发送给您自己的服务器（经过身份验证的 POST 到您的发件箱），并且您的服务器进行排队、以指数退避重试并遵循“重试后”。 承认SMTP的MUA/MSA/MTA分离是正确的。 电子邮件的巧妙之处之一是，如果目标服务器出现故障，您的服务器会重试数天，然后您就会忘记它。

但让我们添加一个 SMTP 从未有过的改进。 每条消息都带有一个 ID，该 ID 是其内容的哈希值，因此重试是幂等的。 接收服务器通过 ID 进行重复数据删除，经典的“由于 ACK 失败而导致重复的电子邮件”通过构建而消失。

交付的完整周期，目标节点在第一次尝试时关闭：

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Ana as Ana's client
    participant SA as Ana's server
    participant SB as Bob's server

    Ana->>SA: POST /outbox (signed message)
    SA-->>Ana: 202 queued
    SA->>SB: GET /.well-known/hmtp/bob
    SB-->>SA: Bob's inbox and keys
    SA->>SB: POST /hmtp/inbox/bob (envelope + sealed body)
    Note over SB: down: no response
    Note over SA: queue: retries with exponential backoff
    SA->>SB: POST /hmtp/inbox/bob (retry, same id)
    SB->>SA: GET /.well-known/hmtp/ana
    SA-->>SB: Ana's signing key
    Note over SB: signature verified, deduplicated by id
    SB-->>SA: 201 delivered

请注意，该图包含整个协议：.wellknown 的两个 GET 是发现和验证，POST 是传递，队列位于发送者服务器上应有的位置。

4. 使用我们已有的密钥进行签名和加密

该消息是一个签名对象，而不是松散的文本：

{
  "id": "sha256:9f2c...",
  "from": "ana@example.com",
  "to": ["bruno@example.org"],
  "date": "2026-07-26T10:00:00Z",
  "in_reply_to": "sha256:11ab...",
  "subject": "Re: that idea",
  "body": { "type": "text/markdown", "content": "<encrypted>" },
  "signature": "..."
}

这给我们带来了很多东西：

  • 静态真实性：存储的邮件带有其加密证明。 转发者保留原始签名。 即使通过转发链，伪造发送者也是不可能的。
  • 无需 DKIM 的发件人验证：接收服务器获取来自域的 .wellknown 并检查密钥签名。 和Webmention验证的动作是一样的。 证据是从源头获取的。
  • E2E：发现文档公开加密密钥（X25519）；本体采用 HPKE 密封。 信封（发件人、收件人、id、日期）对于路由和过滤保持可见；内容仅供收件人使用。
  • 线程：in_reply_to 和内容哈希引用。 无需启发式即可重建对话。
  • 附件：邮件外。 附件是指向发件人服务器的{hash, url, size}；接收者按需下载它，他们的服务器可以镜像它。 不再有 Base64 膨胀的邮箱。

5. 分层反垃圾邮件

与任何系统一样，这是一个复杂的问题，需要多层防御。 对于 HMTP，我们可以从三个开始：

  1. 身份成本：以 ana@example.com 身份签名需要在 example.com 上提供密钥文档。 身份锚定于域名，而域名需要花钱。 这是自签名身份所没有的女巫成本。 但是，域为您提供了无限的子域和邮箱，因此成本会减慢独立身份（而不是地址）的大规模创建速度。 我们在根部层面开展工作。
  2. 首次联系同意：未知发件人不会进入邮箱；他们降落在“请求”框中，其中第一条消息可见（如 Signal 的消息请求）。 您接受，该线程将永远打开。 陌生人可以敲你的门，这是邮件的基本属性，但他们不能填满你的客厅。
  3. 陌生人可选邮资：服务器可以回复 402 的第一次联系。 每个邮箱均可配置；冷垃圾邮件的成本不再为零。

6. 阅读也被指定

电子邮件标准化发送 (SMTP) 和阅读 (IMAP/POP) 作为独立的世界。 我们不需要发明任何东西：通过 JSON/HTTP 读取、同步和搜索邮箱已经由 IETF 解决和标准化。 它称为 JMAP。 HMTP 将定义交付；读取的是带有一种新对象类型的 JMAP。 使用SSE或WebPush推送到客户端。 完整的周期（发送、交付、读取、同步）保留在 HTTP 上。

结论

电子邮件的每个问题都有一个已部署且有效的解决方案：Mastodon 中的发现、ActivityPub 中的传递、IndieWeb 中的验证、Bluesky 中的可轮换身份、Fastmail 中的阅读、Signal 中的同意。 电子邮件的升级已经存在，但没有人组装它。

我们通过优雅、现代的解决方案解决了许多问题：

  • 声誉和社交许可（SPF、DKIM、DMARC、反向 PTR、阻止列表、IP 预热数月）：由每条消息的加密验证、一个签名和一个 GET 到发件人的 .well-known 所取代。 可以验证的财产不需要声誉。
  • 发件人欺骗：通过构造不可能实现。 接收方根据发件人域上发布的密钥检查签名，即使在转发时，签名也会随消息一起传输。
  • 邮件委托（MX 记录）：.wellknown 中的静态文档，具有每个用户委托且没有 DNS 更改。
  • 内容隐私（没有人花时间配置的 PGP）：默认端到端加密；接收服务器存储它无法读取的正文。
  • 垃圾邮件（事后统计过滤器）：首次接触同意（陌生人敲门，他们不会走进邮箱），锚定到域的昂贵身份，以及 402 的可选邮资。
  • 重试时重复：消息 ID 是其内容的哈希值，因此重试是幂等的，并且接收者通过构造来消除重复。
  • 使用启发式重建线程：in_reply_to 指向父消息的哈希值；对话是一个可验证的图表。
  • 轻型邮箱：通过引用附件（哈希+ URL），按需下载。
  • 简单、熟悉的基础设施：一切都通过标准 HTTPS 传输，位于同一个 Nginx 和已经为您的网站提供服务的同一个证书后面。
  • 密钥轮换（DKIM 的操作噩梦）：一个命令。 由于没有人固定您的密钥，因此新密钥会立即受到信任，而被盗的密钥也会很快变得毫无用处。

空谈是廉价的，所以我用 Python 实现了一个工作原型：github.com/tanrax/hmtp。 全部在一个文件中。 该原型涵盖了完整的传输：签名交付、源验证、端到端加密、首次接触同意、重复数据删除、线程、具有指数退避的队列和一个命令中的密钥轮换。 它故意忽略了外围的部分：签名轮换链（接收者在每次交付时实时获取您的密钥而不是固定它，因此只有在节点缓存密钥后该链才开始付款）、402 邮资、引用附件和 JMAP 读取。 自述文件包含快速入门（两分钟内的第一条消息，给自己发送邮件）、在计算机上交换加密邮件的两个节点的演示，以及从 DNS 到 systemd 的完整生产指南。 请记住，这是一个未经审计的密码学设计实验；不要将其用于任何人依赖的秘密。 尽管它可能是一个轻量级的通信系统，适用于您想到的任何生态系统。

我希望您旅途愉快。 如果您发送了第一条 HMTP 消息，我很想听听。
